chunks: And I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His Messenger
whom He deputed at a time when people were moving in an abyss and surging in bewilderment. The reins of destruction were leading them, and the locks of malice were fixed upon their hearts.

key_terms.أَقْفَالُ الرَّيْنِ: Locks of malice or seal of stubbornness
key_terms.غَمْرَةٍ: Abyss or deep water, metaphorically representing deep ignorance or confusion

ai.seo_question: What was the spiritual state of humanity before the Prophet Muhammad's mission according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi frames this description within the Shia concept of *Jahiliyyah* not merely as ignorance but as an active state of spiritual entrapment, where the 'reins of destruction' signify the dominance of tribalism and false deities. This passage underscores the Prophet's role as the divine guide who unlocked the sealed hearts, a theme central to Ali ibn Abi Talib's (AS) sermons emphasizing the transition from chaos to divine order through the Imamate.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I stand witness that Muḥammad — the peace and blessing of Allāh be upon him and his descendants — is His slave and His Messenger
whom He deputed (at a time) when people were collecting in the abyss and moving in bewilderment. The reins of destruction were dragging them, and the locks of malice lay fixed on their hearts.
